subject: PHTH
title: Introduction to Professional Practice 1
description: Physical therapy and its domains through promoting health and well-being of individuals across the life span.

subject: PHTH
title: Sports Medicine Practicum
description: This course is intended to provide students with a directed, practical experience in pre-event, on-field and post-event sports therapy interventions. Students will be introduced to current concepts in sports medicine. Students will work closely with at least one of the McGill varsity teams, as well as intra- and interprofessionally with the staff of the McGill Sport Medicine Clinic (including physiotherapists, athletic therapists, physicians, and other allied health-care professionals).

prerequisites.text: PHTH 245; ANAT 315; PHGY 209; ANAT 316; PHGY 210; POTH 225; POTH 250. Students require a valid CPR-AED level HCP certificate before the practical work begins. Required interviews and selection process for this course will be conducted by the McGill Sport Medicine Clinic staff.

restrictions.text: Only open to U2 of the B.Sc. (Rehabilitation Science) students.

notes: Team allocation will be determined after the interview according to interview performance, availability and student interests.

subject: PHTH
title: Clinical Exercise Physiology
description: Safe and effective prescription of exercise as a preventive and therapeutic tool in patients suffering from clinical conditions.

restrictions.text: Open only to PT students - School of Physical & Occupational Therapy.

subject: PHTH
title: Introduction to PT Clinical Practice
description: In this course, students will be introduced to clinical skills applicable to various physiotherapy domains of practice. Through clinical skills laboratories, self-directed learning, and interactive learning sessions, students will be developing observation skills, as well as analyzing normal and common deviant movements. They will also be introduced to the development of hypotheses to explain movement impairment. Throughout the course, emphasis will be put on palpation and patient handling skills.

prerequisites.text: PHTH 245 and POTH 250

restrictions.text: Open only to PT students - School of Physical & Occupational Therapy

subject: PHTH
title: Introduction to Functional Movement
description: Introduction to the assessment and instruction of human functional movement patterns, including anatomy, physiology, and biomechanics. Principles of progressive functional resistance training.

prerequisites.text: ANAT 315, ANAT 323, POTH 225, PHTH 440

restrictions.text: Open only to U2 students in the B.Sc.(Rehab.Sc.); Major in Physical Therapy program.

subject: PHTH
title: Introduction to Health, Fitness and Lifestyle
description: Introduction to lifestyle concepts and practices, complementary to the scope of physiotherapy practice, which influence individual health and fitness. Topics include: physical activity, sedentary behaviour, diet, sleep, and psychological and mental wellbeing. Certain external factors that influence these concepts and practices, and approaches to promoting behavioural change.

restrictions.text: Open only to U2 students in the B.Sc.(Rehab.Sc.); Major in Physical Therapy program.

subject: PHTH
title: Physical Therapy Clinical Practicum Seminars
description: How the seven entry to practice domains play out in clinical practice, including the resources available while on placement. The clinical education program requirements and preparatory activities, feedback and conflict management, the evaluation process concerning practice domains, the role of the Ordre professionnel de la Physiotherapie du Québec, and different associations in physiotherapy.

restrictions.text: Open to Bachelor of Science(Rehabilitation Science); Major in Physical Therapy U3 students and Qualifying Year for the Master of Science(Applied) in Physical Therapy; Non-Thesis students.

notes: Students must register for both PHTH 505D1 and PHTH 505D2.
No credit will be given for this course unless both PHTH 505D1 and PHTH 505D2 are successfully completed in consecutive terms

subject: PHTH
title: Physical Therapy Orthopedic Management
description: Evaluation and treatment in a neuromuscular framework.

prerequisites.text: ANAT 315 or EDKP 206 or equivalent, EDKP 395 or equivalent as judged by the admission process

subject: PHTH
title: Physical Therapy Neurological Rehabilitation
description: Principles of neurorehabilitation motor learning and neuroplasticity including assessment and treatment.

prerequisites.text: ANAT 321, POTH 455. Restriction: Not open to students who have taken OCC1 335 and PHTH 338.

restrictions.text: Prerequisites: ANAT 321, POTH 455. Restriction: Not open to students who have taken OCC1 335 and PHTH 338.

subject: PHTH
title: PT Cardiorespiratory Rehabilitation
description: Introduction to the principles of cardiorespiratory physical therapy. Students will gain the necessary theoretical knowledge pertaining to the pathophysiology of various medical and surgical respiratory conditions as well as the practical skills needed for evaluating and treating such acute and chronic conditions. This course introduces students to the clinical decision making process involved in the planning, implementation and progression of a cardiorespiratory physiotherapy treatment program.

prerequisites.text: ANAT 316, PHTH 225, PHTH 440, PHGY 209, or equivalent as judged by the admission process.

subject: PHTH
title: Integrated Orthopedic Management
description: Assessment and treatment of patients with multiple comorbidities or multiple injuries that require a multidisciplinary approach, integrated intervention strategies, life-style changes, integration into the work force and/or reintegration into the community.

prerequisites.text: PHTH 550.

subject: PHTH
title: Integrated Neurological Rehabilitation
description: PT assessment and treatment of clients with complex problems and/or multiple handicaps.

prerequisites.text: PHTH 551

subject: PHTH
title: Integrated Cardiorespiratory Rehabilitation
description: Building on previously learned knowledge of cardiorespiratory physiotherapy, students will gain conceptual and procedural knowledge and skills for the physiotherapy assessment and management of patients with various cardiovascular and respiratory conditions, patients undergoing lung/heart-lung transplantation, and critically ill patients managed in the intensive care unit (ICU). This course aims to enhance critical thinking and problem-solving skills in the area of cardiovascular and respiratory physiotherapy through interactive lectures as well as case-based labs run at the McGill Simulation center.

prerequisites.text: PHTH 554 or permission from the instructor.

subject: PHTH
title: PT Clinical Practicum 1
description: A first clinical practicum course.

prerequisites.text: PHTH 550, PHTH 551, PHTH 552 (or PHTH 554 and PHTH 564), PHTH 560, PHTH 561.

subject: PHTH
title: PT Clinical Practicum 2
description: A second clinical practicum including advanced skills in assessment and treatment management in a core area of practice.

prerequisites.text: PHTH 571

notes: **Due to the length of the clinical course, add/drop is the sixth lecture day and withdrawal is the eleventh lecture day.

subject: PHTH
title: PT Clinical Practicum 3
description: Advanced assessment and treatment management in an area of practice.

prerequisites.text: PHTH 571, PHTH 572

subject: PHTH
title: Introduction to Pediatric Physical Therapy
description: This course introduces the principles of pediatric habilitation and rehabilitation pertinent to the practice of physical therapy.

prerequisites.text: Successful completion of the QY/U3 PT year.

restrictions.text: Restricted to MSc.(A) PT M1 students.

subject: PHTH
title: PT Clinical Practicum 4
description: Final clinical practicum in an area of practice.

prerequisites.text: PHTH 571, PHTH 572, PHTH 573

subject: PHTH
title: Integrated Pain Management
description: This M1 entry-level physiotherapy course focuses on understanding and managing complex and chronic pain conditions. Through lectures, personal reflection, interactive class activities, case study analyses, quizzes, assignments and practical lab activities, students will develop a conceptual framework for approaching the clinical assessment and management of pain and pain-related disability. By the end of the course, students will be ready to apply this framework within clinical settings.

prerequisites.text: Clinical Affiliation 1 & 2 or permission of instructor. PHTH 552 (or PHTH 554 and PHTH 564), PHTH 561.

subject: PHTH
title: Differential Diagnosis and Management
description: Building on previously learned orthopaedic knowledge, screening for medical conditions and establishing functional differential diagnosis.

prerequisites.text: PHTH 550, PHTH 560.

subject: PHTH
title: X-Ray Prescription for Physical Therapy
description: Requirements for X-ray prescription described by the Québec Code des Professions (chapter M-9, r. 4).

restrictions.text: Open only to students in the M.Sc.(A.) in Physical Therapy; Non-Thesis program.

subject: PHTH
title: Pelvic Floor Rehabilitation
description: This course explores the physiotherapy approach to pelvic floor disorders, with an in-depth focus on urinary incontinence. Students will understand the role of the pelvic floor in relation to urinary, sexual and ano-rectal function, and acquire the ability to evaluate and treat patients suffering urinary incontinence.

prerequisites.text: PHTH 623

restrictions.text: Open to students in the MSc (A) in Physical Therapy. Open to other students by permission of instructor only.

subject: PHTH
title: Integrated Clinical Exercise Rehabilitation
description: This case-based course aims to provide students with an in-depth knowledge of exercise rehabilitation as a preventative and therapeutic tool in patients with selective chronic diseases and disabilities across the lifespan. This course aims to enhance critical thinking and problem-solving skills through interactive lectures, clinical reasoning workshops and assignments.

prerequisites.text: PHTH 440 and PHTH 552 (or PHTH 554 and PHTH 564).

restrictions.text: Restricted to MSc(A) PT M1 Students.

subject: PHTH
title: Sport Physiotherapy
description: Injury prevention for recreational and elite athletes and rehabilitation of injured athletes.

prerequisites.text: PHTH 623

subject: PHTH
title: Advanced Manual Therapy
description: Use of manual therapy in the assessment and treatment of patients with musculoskeletal disorders.

prerequisites.text: PHTH 551, PHTH 552 (or PHTH 554 and PHTH 564) , PHTH 623
